R02.text: Over your 28-day baseline you averaged ~471 min of sleep (starting ~22:50, ending 07:00), ~7,998 steps/day, and ~55 active minutes/day. During the recent 14 days, your sleep timing and duration remained stable (~469 min), as did resting heart rate (~56 bpm) and HRV (~45 ms). However, daily steps fell to ~2,321 and recorded active minutes dropped sharply from ~55 to ~5 min/day, with several days showing zero or near-zero activity. Low-movement minutes were essentially unchanged. Your cardiovascular metrics at rest appear steady, but the near-absence of detected active minutes represents a substantial change in recorded daytime movement worth reviewing.

R03.text: During the 28-day baseline, metrics were stable with full wear: sleep ~471 min ending at 07:00, steps ~7998, activity ~55 min, low movement ~451 min, resting HR ~56.1 bpm, and RMSSD ~45.3 ms. In the 14-day window, steps fell abruptly to ~2321/day (−71%) and activity to ~5 min/day (from ~55 min), persisting throughout. Sleep remained near ~469 min with unchanged timing. Low movement (~448 min), resting HR (~56.3 bpm), and RMSSD (~44.8 ms) were stable. The step and activity reductions were continuous without recovery; other metrics were unaffected.

R04.text: Your recent 14 days show a striking change in daytime movement. Steps fell from a baseline average of ~7,998 to ~2,321 per day, and recorded active minutes dropped from ~55 to ~5 daily, with several days at zero. Despite this, sleep duration remained stable (~469 vs ~471 min), always ending at 07:00. Resting heart rate (~56 bpm) and RMSSD (~45 ms) were unchanged. Low-movement minutes stayed near ~448–451. This suggests either a major routine shift or a device-recording difference affecting step and activity detection while sleep and heart metrics continued normally.

R09.text: During the 28-day baseline, sleep averaged 471 min (start ~22:50, end 07:00), steps ~7998/day, activity ~55 min, RHR ~56 bpm, RMSSD ~45 ms. In the 14-day window, sleep timing and duration remained stable (mean 469 min). Steps dropped markedly to ~2321/day (-71%). Activity minutes fell from ~55 to ~5/day, with several zero-activity days. Low movement (~448), RHR (~56), and RMSSD (~45) were unchanged. Patterns persisted across weekdays and weekends without recovery. Baseline step-activity correlation was weak; window correlations remained negligible.
